system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Rouse Properties, Inc. realized record, ~2015-2017 horizon

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The outcome window is fixed at construction to
> the ~3-5-year record following the ~2012 closing (~2015-2017). The company was acquired
> whole and deregistered mid-2016, so the public record bounds at that point; facts below
> are drawn only from the realized post-closing record. This sub-dossier contains no
> information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Realized annual financial record (last full public year)
- For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015 the company reported net income of $41,623 thousand, following net losses in each of the prior reported years: $(51,685) thousand (2014), $(54,745) thousand (2013), $(68,659) thousand (2012) and $(26,976) thousand (2011). [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-16-012359, Form 10-K FY2015]
- Net income (loss) allocable to common shareholders was $40,746 thousand for 2015, versus $(51,756) thousand for 2014; basic earnings per share allocable to common shareholders was $0.70 for 2015 versus $(0.90) for 2014. [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-16-012359, Form 10-K FY2015]
- The FY2015 net income included a $26,558 thousand gain on extinguishment of debt; the company stated it had "a history of prior net losses" and could not assure "sustained profitability going forward." [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-16-012359, Form 10-K FY2015]

## Realized ownership outcome (whole-company acquisition and deregistration)
- On July 6, 2016 (the "Effective Time") the company completed a merger with BSREP II Retail Holdings Corp., a wholly owned subsidiary of BSREP II Retail Pooling LLC and an affiliate of Brookfield Asset Management Inc. ("Brookfield"), whereby the company became a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent; the merger was effected pursuant to an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated February 25, 2016. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-131198, Form 8-K (July 6, 2016)]
- At the Effective Time each outstanding share of company common stock was converted into the right to receive $18.25 in cash (other than shares held by Brookfield-affiliated Exchange Parties, Parent, Acquisition Sub, the Guarantors, and dissenting shares perfecting appraisal rights). [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-131198, Form 8-K (July 6, 2016)]
- On July 6, 2016 the company requested that the NYSE suspend trading and withdraw the common stock from listing; the common stock was to be delisted on July 18, 2016, and the company stated it intended to file a Form 15 to deregister under the Exchange Act and suspend its reporting obligations. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-131198, Form 8-K (July 6, 2016)]
- The company filed a Form 15-12B on July 18, 2016 to certify termination of registration / suspend reporting duties for the common stock. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-132940, Form 15-12B]

## Realized management / organizational record at the interface
- In connection with the merger and at the Effective Time, President and Chief Executive Officer Andrew Silberfein resigned as CEO and as a director, and Chief Financial Officer John Wain resigned; the termination of both was without cause. Brian Kingston (previously sole director of Acquisition Sub) continued as the company's sole director. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-131198, Form 8-K (July 6, 2016)]
- On July 8, 2016 Rouse Properties, Inc. was converted into a limited liability company named "Rouse Properties, LLC" (as successor in interest to Rouse Properties, Inc.). [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-132441, Form 8-K (July 8, 2016)]

## No-record note (window bound)
- Because the company was acquired whole by Brookfield in July 2016 and deregistered under the Exchange Act, no separate public annual report exists for the later part of the fixed ~2015-2017 window (no FY2016 or FY2017 10-K). The acquirer did not separately disclose the acquired business's standalone trajectory in a public periodic report retrievable here. The realized public record therefore bounds at the FY2015 10-K and the July 2016 acquisition/deregistration; any post-mid-2016 standalone operating trajectory is [UNVERIFIED]. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-132940, Form 15-12B]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The entity operated as a standalone public company from the ~2012 distribution through mid-2016, reporting net losses each year from 2011 through 2014 and its first reported annual net income ($41.6 million) in FY2015 (aided by a $26.6 million debt-extinguishment gain), before being acquired whole by an affiliate of Brookfield on July 6, 2016 at $18.25 per share in cash, delisted, converted to an LLC, and deregistered — with the incumbent CEO and CFO departing at closing; no separate public outcome record exists for the remainder of the fixed window (coded bounded/uncertain beyond mid-2016 per the no-record rule). [SRC: SEC accession 0001628280-16-012359, Form 10-K FY2015] [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-131198, Form 8-K (July 6, 2016)] [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-16-132940, Form 15-12B]

[SLICE END]
